main_results.result: New candidate changes next-ADMIT recovery authority from historical_close to provenance-aware closeprov while retaining one exact attempt module per process epoch.

All declared exact siblings were byte-verified and executed through no-stub ADMIT/RESERVE/SCORE/SLOT/COMMIT/CLOSE/replay, two fresh context epochs, fail-closed two-slot crash recovery, and integrated torn-frame checks.

new_defect.name: v1_next_admit_uses_stale_historical_replay_authority
new_defect.reproduction: After a runtime-provenance contracted block is closed with reservation_compliance_close_replay_runtime_provenance_2026-08-28.py, the v1 ProcessStableRuntimeContext passes historical_close into the next ADMIT recovery. Exact replay fails with ComplianceCloseError: compliance CLOSE reporting binding mismatch.
new_defect.repair: Use closeprov as the ADMIT compliance/replay authority. Exact two-block execution across fresh context epochs then succeeds with reporting prefixes 1 and 2.

validated_contracts: Exact no-stub stable lifecycle: ADMIT -> RESERVE -> SCORE -> bound SLOT -> recovery COMMIT -> runtime-provenance CLOSE -> replay produces the intended scientific score with exactly one scorer call.
The first process-epoch permit remains invalid in a freshly loaded context; durable fail-closed recovery still permits COMMIT reconstruction from a durable bound SLOT without scorer relaunch.
Two fresh context epochs can close consecutive runtime-contracted blocks when next-ADMIT replay uses closeprov; final reporting history contains both rows and clean EOF.
If a stochastic score is generated but its bound SLOT is not durable before crash, a fresh epoch never relaunches it and the planned slot contributes fail-closed score=1.

All 933 proper SLOT-frame cuts, 357 COMMIT-frame cuts and 2545 CLOSE-frame cuts collapsed to the prior valid prefix with zero prefix-contract violations. Representative stable-sidecar repair produced fail-closed missing SLOT, recovery-commit for durable SLOT, and safe re-CLOSE respectively.
measurement_validity_rules: Versioned replay authority must advance with the write format. A component that can emit a newer scientific CLOSE format cannot use an older replay authority when authorizing later work.

Process-local launch permits are intentionally non-transferable across fresh process epochs under the current _BOOT_SECRET design. This is a scientific execution-affinity constraint, not just an implementation detail.
Durable SLOT is the evidence boundary. Precrash scorer execution without a durable SLOT must not be inferred, recovered, retried, or selected post hoc.
Crash recovery may reconstruct sidecar COMMIT only from a unique durable SLOT whose reservation/attempt binding is exact; it may not regenerate score evidence.
scope_limitations: Single-host cooperative POSIX only; StableSidecarJournalIO is not a distributed fencing mechanism.
Scalar deterministic scorers validate lifecycle semantics but do not measure real LLM runtime latency or quality.
The v2 candidate intentionally focuses on the tested lifecycle surface; API-parity with every convenience method exposed by v1 is not yet certified.
No claim is made that process-local permit affinity is suitable for a multi-process scorer architecture.
frontier: Restore and test API parity for the ordinary non-crash COMMIT path in a superseding context candidate, without weakening the already-validated recovery path.

Characterize the process-affinity contract explicitly: prove that a permit issued in one process cannot authorize scoring in another, then compare same-process scoring, deterministic replay, and any proposed cross-process authorization without allowing old permits to survive a process-epoch fence.

Run a full multiprocessing race campaign through StableSidecarJournalIO with exact context loading: duplicate ADMIT, duplicate RESERVE for one slot, and stale append/CAS races. Require at most one durable reservation and at most one authorized scorer launch.

Add a late-SLOT versus deadline-CLOSE race campaign and verify that scheduling order can affect completion/fail-closed status but cannot create duplicate scientific evidence or bypass runtime provenance.
Only after those single-host races are closed, explore an explicit distributed-fencing design if multi-host execution is actually required.
exact_next_action: Create a small superseding context with ordinary prepare_commit API parity and run the normal non-crash path. Then launch 4-8 cooperating processes against the same stable-sidecar main/ledger paths, each with independently loaded exact context, to race duplicate ADMIT and duplicate RESERVE. Record durable winners, CAS losers, scorer-call authorization count, and process-affinity failures without introducing any shared secret that survives a fresh process epoch.
